partnershipPlan: Two patient partners review the checklist wording before cycle 1 and the night rules before cycle 2; one night-shift nurse and the ward pharmacist join the huddle debrief each fortnight.
socialListening: No social media listening; the ward's patient comment cards from the last six months are read for mentions of medicines at shift change.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Nobody told me the blood thinner had been stopped until the night nurse came round with it again.
items.implication: Name same-day stopped medicines explicitly in the medicines section.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I sit with my father every evening and I would have caught that, if anyone had said it out loud.
items.implication: Invite a family member who is present to the bedside check when the patient agrees.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Two of us for sixteen patients; if it takes more than a couple of minutes each it will stop after the first week.
items.implication: Keep the checklist under two minutes and track duration as a balancing measure.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Half of what I chase in the morning was already known at seven in the evening; it just was not passed on.
items.implication: Add items pending from pharmacy to the medicines section and use pharmacist-found discrepancies as a cross-check.

summary: Four composite voices shaping the checklist content, the night rule and the measurement cross-check.
